*Answers any question about any skill in this repo — setup, usage, commands, architecture, troubleshooting — from an index built out of the skills' own files, and says so plainly when the answer is not in there.*

> **Never answer ungrounded: every fact this skill emits carries the file and line it was read from, a fact that loses its source is dropped rather than shown, and a question the cards cannot ground is answered by the retrieval command's own not-documented block — naming which skills and sections were searched — never by prose written to fill the gap.**

## Why install this

Seventeen skills live in this repo, each with its own setup, its own commands
and its own refusals. The documentation for all of them exists — spread across
seventeen `SKILL.md` files, seventeen READMEs and seventeen invariant
declarations. Finding the one line you need means knowing which of those files
it is in.

This turns that into a question you can ask. It extracts an index from the
skills' own files — five fixed sections per skill, every fact carrying the
`file:line` it came from — and answers out of it in one command.

**The reason to trust it is that it refuses.** Ask something the index cannot
ground and it returns `NOT DOCUMENTED`, naming what it searched and what it
found nearest, rather than a plausible paragraph. An answer here is always
checkable, which is the one thing a general answer about your own tooling can
never be.

Adding a skill needs no maintenance: `ci / skillhelp` runs against `skills/**`
and fails when any card **would change**, so a new or edited skill surfaces as a
red check with one command to fix it.

## What you get

| Path | What it provides |
|---|---|
| `skills/skillhelp/SKILL.md` | What the agent reads: triggers, the flow, and the one rule. |
| `skills/skillhelp/scripts/` | The deterministic half — `build`, `check`, `ask`, `list`. |
| `skills/skillhelp/references/anatomy.md` | The fixed shape of a card — the five sections, what each is extracted from, and the file:line grounding every fact must carry. |
| `skills/skillhelp/references/answering.md` | How to answer from retrieved facts: citation form, when to relay the not-documented block verbatim, and the refusal to fill a gap with plausible prose. |
| `skills/skillhelp/references/extraction.md` | Which file each section is read out of per stack, why Troubleshooting weights the invariants prose and the non-negotiable rules over changelog lines, the secret-shaped-line refusal, and the fallbacks when a skill does not ship a source. |
| `skills/skillhelp/skill-invariants.json` | The prose guardrails and the baseline eval declaration. |

## Quick start

```bash
# ask a question — one command, sources included
skillhelp ask "how do I set up ghostwriter"
skillhelp ask "what commands does press have"
skillhelp ask "why is my release not cutting a tag"

skillhelp list    # the catalogue: every skill, version, trigger phrases
skillhelp check   # fail if any card would change (this is the CI gate)
skillhelp build   # rewrite the cards after a skill changes
```

Install from the [claude-skills marketplace](https://github.com/natejswenson/claude-skills), then ask
for work matching the triggers below.

## Triggers

- "/skillhelp"
- "how do I use <skill>"
- "how do I set up <skill>"
- "what commands does <skill> have"
- "what does <skill> do"
- "how does <skill> work"
- "why is <skill> failing"
- "what skills do I have"
- "which skill should I use for"
- "explain <skill> to me"
- "document my skills"
- "rebuild the skill index"
- Anything the method in `SKILL.md` covers, whether or not it is phrased that way.

## Requirements

- Node 18+ (the bundled scripts are ESM, no dependencies).

## Development

```bash
cd skills/skillhelp/skills/skillhelp
npm test
```

Node skill. `ci / skillhelp` runs the same tests plus the house lints on
every pull request, and `skillfactory verify --skill skillhelp` reports which rung
of the ladder it has reached.
